surface: taskful-day — microsite /apps/taskful-day/ (Persuade) + /apps/taskful-day/privacy/, /apps/taskful-day/support/ and the alternatives pages that target it: /alternatives/streaks-app/, /alternatives/habitica/, /alternatives/habitnow/, /alternatives/productive/, /alternatives/way-of-life/ (Read variants)

dossier.mechanism: Taskful Day plans one day at a time: you pick from the inbox what belongs in today, see that plan in four shapes (Day Clock, Energy River, Day Map, Focus Orbit), work it in Focus Orbit sessions (25-minute default), and whatever is unfinished rolls forward to tomorrow as a follow-up — no streak, no red badge, no reset — while the same day stays in step on iPhone, iPad and Mac through the user's own iCloud under one Universal Purchase.
dossier.audienceScene: People who uninstalled streak apps after one missed day, people with ADHD or variable schedules who need a realistic day rather than a backlog, and Mac desk workers who plan at the desk and capture on the phone. They arrive on a phone from Google or an AI answer ('daily planner Mac', 'ADHD planner app', 'Streaks alternative', 'calm to do list') or on desktop at the start of the work day, where the app must reach the iPhone via QR. The developer's own scene (journal): three tasks planned at the coffee maker in the kitchen, nine wanted at the desk, the planner open in a corner of the Mac for eight hours. The app uses European dot times (20.15).
dossier.culturalHome: Paper day-planning and focus rituals, not SaaS dashboards: the to-do card or list on the desk, the Ivy Lee 'six things for tomorrow' card, the bullet-journal migration arrow, the tear-off day calendar, the Pomodoro kitchen timer. The studio's own vocabulary from its essays: 'follow-ups' not failures, 'week-three trust', 'a streak counter is a debt the user owes the app'.
dossier.mustProve: In the first viewport: the plan is today only and an unfinished task visibly moves on to tomorrow with no penalty (the screenshot's Call dentist 20.15 against three finished tasks); native on iPhone, iPad and Mac with one Universal Purchase; the honest price line from price.value 'Free — Pro from $2.99/mo' ($24.99/yr, $39.99 lifetime in plans); the official App Store badge in working form, plus the QR on desktop.
dossier.categoryDefault: Productivity SaaS: white page, blue/purple gradient, checkmark logo, split hero with iPhone mockup, 'Get more done' copy, four icon feature cards, highlighted annual plan, star testimonials. The app's own UI (pale sky gradient, iOS system blue #007AFF, frosted cards, SF Pro) and its glossy icon (calendar page, blue check, sun glow) already sit in this rut.
dossier.predictableOpposite: Calm-wellness: cream page, serif display, soft pastel blobs, sunrise gradients, rounded illustrations and 'mindful' copy (the incumbent Paper & Ink and the AI prior) — or a near-black focus dashboard with a glowing timer ring.
dossier.literalReading: 'Taskful Day' plus the icon read literally is a calendar day-page with a check on it: the tear-off day calendar (candidate 4, the only one that uses it). The Pomodoro tomato is the literal reading of Focus Orbit; candidate 6 keeps the timer but refuses the tomato.

candidates.name: Tomorrow's Card — the ruled 3×5 index card (Ivy Lee's six-things card, the binder-clipped 'Hipster PDA' stack)
candidates.why: The to-do card is on every desk, and the planning audience knows the Ivy Lee story by heart. It carries the mechanism exactly: one card physically limits a day to a realistic size, and anything unfinished is rewritten onto tomorrow's card under an arrow.

candidates.name: The Ticket Rail — thermal task tickets (the ADHD receipt-printer to-do practice, kitchen ticket rail and spike)
candidates.family: service counter / thermal print and steel
candidates.why: The ADHD audience spread this practice themselves around 2024: one printed ticket per task makes starting physical. It carries the mechanism directly: a voice capture prints a ticket, finished tickets go on the spike, and unfinished ones are re-clipped on tomorrow's rail.

candidates.name: Sunny Hours Only — the wall or garden sundial and its motto 'Horas non numero nisi serenas'
candidates.why: It is the best-known clock motto, and it states the studio's anti-streak ethic in four words. It carries the mechanism: the gnomon's shadow marks 'now' on a Day Clock, and a missed or cloudy hour leaves no mark at all.

candidates.name: The Tear-Off Day — the desk block calendar (Abreißkalender, himekuri), the literal reading of the icon
candidates.why: One sheet is one day, and everyone has torn one off. It carries the mechanism: tearing today's sheet reveals tomorrow with the unfinished task already printed on it. Saturday-blue and Sunday-red weekdays are the real convention.

candidates.name: The Letterboard — the felt letterboard with push-in letters from cafés and kitchens
candidates.why: It is the everyday ritual of putting up a 'today' message. It carries the mechanism: a fixed number of rows makes a realistic day, letters picked from the tray are the inbox, and tomorrow you rearrange the board without wiping it.

candidates.name: The Wind-Up Timer — the 60-minute kitchen dial timer behind the Pomodoro Technique (Cirillo, late 1980s)
candidates.why: It is the best-known focus object in productivity and carries Focus Orbit's 25-minute default directly. A timer keeps no record, so every wind is a fresh start. The rollover only works if the dial grammar is extended to the 24-hour day.

candidates.name: Now Showing — the changeable-letter cinema marquee and its box office
candidates.why: Its link to planning is the weakest, but everyone knows a marquee. It carries the mechanism: today's programme becomes the showtimes, and 'HELD OVER', the cinema's own phrase for a run that simply continues, sits next to 'COMING TOMORROW'.

styles.label: Held Over
styles.lineage: The changeable-letter marquee of a neighbourhood single-screen cinema. Its parts: a backlit translucent attraction board with horizontal letter tracks; black and coloured slotted letters hung by hand each day with a pole (zip-change letters, US, from the 1930s); chaser-bulb borders; a structural-glass fascia; lit poster cases along the entrance; a box office with a speaking grille and a ticket tray. Its vocabulary: NOW SHOWING, TODAY ONLY, HELD OVER (a run kept on because it is still going), COMING TOMORROW, ADMISSION, running time.
styles.thesis: Today is the only feature on the bill. The page is a cinema front whose attraction board carries the day's showtimes, and anything unfinished is HELD OVER to tomorrow in the marquee's own words. It refuses the split hero and the feature-card grid in favour of a working letter board, a box office and an arcade of lit cases.
styles.scene: Someone on the pavement at blue hour, phone in hand, deciding what tomorrow holds under a neighbourhood cinema's lit attraction board, the brightest thing on the street. Dark scheme (color-scheme: dark): blue-hour fascia as the ground, lit white panels as every reading surface.

palette.role: Blue-hour fascia (midnight structural glass): page ground, nav band, frame surrounds. Enamel lettering on it is 14.3:1
Lit panel (cool fluorescent white): attraction board, box office glass, programme and notice panels. Every long reading surface
Letter black: tiles and all body text on lit panels (17:1)
Blue letter (the app's own blue): the HELD OVER track, showtime figures, links on panels (6.0:1). No red letters anywhere, because the app refuses red badges
Bulb amber: flat chaser-bulb dots, focus ring on the fascia (10.1:1), sticky-bar edge
Fascia lettering: nav, captions and headings set directly on the ground
Stainless trim: letter-track rails, case frames, secondary captions on the fascia (7.3:1)

type.display: Big Shoulders Display 800 for the letter tiles: H1, board titles and price-board lines in caps, +0.04em tracking, 80px desktop / 40px mobile on the attraction board. 600 for the fascia name and the four views' names set on panels.
type.text: Cabin 400 for reading copy at 18px/1.6 on lit panels and 17px on the fascia. Cabin 500 for nav, labels, plan names and captions.
type.utility: Big Shoulders Display 600 with tabular figures for showtimes, prices and running time (real data). No mono.
type.rationale: Big Shoulders was drawn for the City of Chicago from its theatre-district and industrial signage. Its tall, flat-sided capitals sit on a tile the way zip-change letters sit on a track, and they stay legible at 18px on a phone. Cabin is a humanist sans modelled on Johnston and Gill, the lettering of interwar cinema fronts, programme leaflets and the transit posters that advertised them, so the reading copy sounds like the cinema's printed programme. About 63 KB in total (2 × 14.5 KB + 2 × 17 KB).

styles.navigation: The nav band carries the brand and links. 'TASKFUL DAY' (icon + name) sits at left and links to the top. Five in-page links in Cabin 500 sit on the fascia at right: Showtimes, Running order, Admission, Questions, Box office (→ #get). A single amber bulb dot before a link marks the current section (aria-current). On mobile, 'Programme' opens a lit panel with the same anchors plus Privacy and Support. The nav does not stick; the mini-marquee download bar is the only sticky element.
styles.signatureInteraction: 'Close today's show': a real <button aria-pressed> on the showtimes board. When pressed, the three finished showings' tiles unhook and drop off the track letter by letter (translateY plus a 6° swing, 18ms stagger). CALL DENTIST 20.15 slides down to the HELD OVER track, and its date tiles re-hang from MON 26 to TUE 27. Pressing 'Reopen Monday' reverses it. Each board has a visually hidden plain-text twin, and the tiles are aria-hidden. No-JS: the board is server-rendered in its final honest state, with the three finished showings in grey 'shown' letters and the HELD OVER track already reading CALL DENTIST 20.15 → TUE 27. Reduced motion: an instant swap with no drop or swing.
styles.motionGrammar: Letters hang rather than fly. When the attraction board and the showtimes board first enter view, their tiles settle onto the tracks with a 2° swing that damps out in 380ms (transform-origin top centre, 14ms per letter); no other region animates on load. The bulbs never chase continuously: a single 700ms chase pass runs around the box office when the badge receives hover or focus. Everything else holds still. With prefers-reduced-motion there is no swing and no chase, and tiles render in place.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy and support: the canopy shrinks to one lit track under the nav band, reading 'TASKFUL DAY · PRIVACY POLICY' or 'TASKFUL DAY · SUPPORT' in 28px tiles. Below it, a single lit reading panel (#F4F6F8, Cabin 400 18px/1.65, 66ch) sits on the midnight ground. The h2s are Big Shoulders 700 26px set as plain type, not tiles. The privacy page opens with the House rules frame and its transparency figures; the support page puts the developer email in a box-office window. Alternatives pages become a DOUBLE FEATURE board ('TASKFUL DAY / STREAKS' on two tracks), with the page's quick_answer as the programme note, the head-to-head table as a two-column programme listing, 'Pick Taskful Day if… / Stick with Streaks if…' as two notice frames, the FAQ rows, and a closing box office with the badge.
styles.assetsNeeded: Nothing new is needed to ship. The tiles are CSS plus Big Shoulders, the bulbs and grille are CSS, and the poster cases use the six existing screenshots. Production follow-ups: screenshots of the four named views and of the Mac app, to replace typeset listings with real posters, and corrected alt text for screenshots 2–6.
styles.risk: This is the lowest-resonance candidate on my list: a cinema is nobody's planner. If bulbs and tiles spread beyond the two boards, the price board and the sticky strip, it will read as theme-park kitsch. The night scene sits next to the 'dark + glowing edges' rut, so there is no blur glow and the bulbs stay flat dots. Tiles read worse than set type, so each board stays at or under 40 characters and every tile string has a plain-text twin. Planning is a morning act; a marquee is an evening one.
styles.memoryTest: The planner whose site was a lit cinema marquee: the unfinished dentist call wasn't a failure, it was 'HELD OVER' to Tuesday, and the App Store badge sat in the box-office ticket tray.

fixes.text: Re-derive every visitorPath from the world's own reading order, and enforce two rules. (1) Within a surface, no two styles may share the relative order of more than two of {price, screenshots, comparison, privacy record, founder, FAQ}. (2) At least one style per surface must change GROUPING, not just order: for example, FAQ split into the sections it answers, who_for/who_not_for folded into the price, or the privacy record as the opener. World-native examples: tare-b sets Puzzle No. 1 before the Rules and puts price and answers at the back like a book. studio-a, allpaid-c and rightsplit-a open with the record (bin label, statement, label data) before any feature. soon-b prints the fare and stub (price) on the face, first. gymlogger-x-c shows the plateau formula before any offer. xiangqiful-c files each FAQ as a margin question on the entry it concerns. observa-b ends on 'past issues' (release notes) instead of a closing CTA block. The maker/freshness line and the shared footer strip may stay common.

Replace it with taskful-day candidate #5, the felt letterboard with push-in letters. It keeps the dealt changeable-letter 'held over' mechanic in a domestic object with no tickets. Set its letters in a face outside the Big Shoulders family, as white letters on a coloured felt rather than amber bulbs on navy.

Add one production task to every style: a one-off script in scripts/ (already excluded from the build, so it is not a deploy build step) that commits derivatives. Icons at 64, 128 and 256px (WebP plus a PNG fallback, about 15 KB or less at 128). Screenshots at 400w, 800w and 1200w WebP (about 40, 90 and 160 KB or less). The studio mark as the clean SVG that studio a/b/c already ask for. Front matter keeps the original paths; one include maps them to the derivatives and emits width/height, srcset/sizes, loading=lazy and decoding=async (eager plus fetchpriority=high only for a single hero image).

Make it a global contract: html { scroll-padding-top: var(--sticky-top); scroll-padding-bottom: var(--sticky-bottom) }, so focus and anchors never land under a bar. Allow one sticky element per edge, pad the bottom bar with env(safe-area-inset-bottom), and on viewports shorter than 600px hide the top strip while the bottom bar is showing.

styles.label: Tomorrow's Card
styles.lineage: The ruled 3×5-inch index card (bright white stock, pale blue rules at a quarter inch, one red header rule) and the Ivy Lee method told since 1918: each evening, write tomorrow's most important tasks on a card, work them in order, and carry anything unfinished to the next day's card. Also the binder-clipped card stack Merlin Mann named the 'Hipster PDA' in 2004, and the A–Z guide cards with staggered tabs found in every card file.
styles.thesis: One card holds one realistic day. The page is a clipped stack of ruled cards on a desk: today's card on top, and tomorrow's next, with the unfinished line already copied across. It refuses the infinite backlog list, the split hero and the icon-card grid.
styles.scene: At the desk beside the Mac in clear morning daylight, writing today's card before the work starts. Light scheme (color-scheme: light): white card stock on a pale ash-grey linoleum desktop.

palette.role: Ash linoleum desk: the page ground around the stack (ink text on it is 9.8:1)
Card stock: every section is a card, and all reading text sits on it
Cyan rule: card rules at 32px pitch that are the page's baseline grid (decorative, not text)
Header rule: the one printed red line under each card's title band (not text, never used as a status colour)
Ballpoint ink: the written layer (H1, task lines, strike marks, carry arrows, links, focus ring). 9.1:1 on white, 5.9:1 on the desk
Graphite: printed text such as the quick answer, FAQ and tables (15:1)
Pencil grey: dates, footnotes and secondary captions (5.8:1)

type.display: Shantell Sans 700 and 500 for the written layer: the H1 at 56px desktop / 34px mobile, card titles at 32px, task lines at 22px, margin dates and arrows. It is never used for paragraphs.
type.text: Inclusive Sans 400 and 600 for the printed layer: body at 18px on a 32px line, locked to the card rules, plus tables, FAQ, and prices in tabular figures.
type.utility: None. Times, prices and counts use Inclusive Sans tabular figures.
type.rationale: An Ivy Lee card is handwritten, but script fonts are costume and hard to read. Shantell Sans is a marker-hand sans engineered by Arrow Type for legibility, with real forms and spacing, so the plan lines look written on the card at no legibility cost. Inclusive Sans was drawn for readability (distinct I/l/1, open apertures, generous spacing), which suits an audience that includes many ADHD and dyslexic readers. It sits under the hand like the card's own printing. About 120 KB (Shantell 2 × 47 KB + Inclusive 2 × 13 KB).

materials: Card stock: flat white rectangles with a 1px #C2C6BF edge and a two-layer soft paper shadow (no hard offset)
Cyan rules at 32px pitch: the global baseline grid, with every line of text sitting on a rule
One red header rule per card, under a 96px title band
Ballpoint ink: strike-through marks on finished lines, the carry arrow '→ Tue', and a hand-drawn SVG loop circling the highlight plan
Binder clip (CSS: a dark steel trapezoid with two wire handles) gripping the stack's top-left corner
Guide cards: staggered tabs rising from the stack's top edge, used as the navigation
Pale ash linoleum desk: a flat matte ground

styles.label: Wound to Twenty-Five
styles.lineage: The mechanical 60-minute kitchen dial timer: the tomato-shaped one Francesco Cirillo used as a student in the late 1980s, which named the Pomodoro Technique, and the coloured-body, black-cap dial timers of European kitchens. Its parts: a printed minute scale with long 5-minute ticks turned against a fixed index; a knurled grip; a moulded body in one colour; the bell at zero; the leaflet ('turn past 10, then set'). A timer keeps no record. Every wind starts from nothing.
styles.thesis: A timer remembers nothing it could hold against you. The page is one wind-up dial seen from above: set it to 25 and the page itself enters Focus Orbit. The day is the same dial at 24-hour scale, carrying what's left past midnight onto the next turn. It refuses the phone-mockup hero, the feature grid and the tomato.
styles.scene: Morning sun on the desk beside the keyboard, with a sun-yellow wind-up timer under a graphite cap seen from directly above, white dial face up. Light scheme (color-scheme: light), drenched in the body colour.

styles.navigation: The knurled graphite cap carries the icon and 'Taskful Day' (brand link to the top) and five in-page links: The day, Leaflet, Pro, Questions, Get it. A small blue index triangle under a link marks the current section (aria-current). On mobile, 'Menu' drops down a white face panel listing the anchors plus Privacy and Support.
styles.signatureInteraction: 'Wind it': the scale ring is a real ARIA slider (role=slider, 5–60 minutes, step 5, default 25), turned by drag, the arrow keys or ± buttons, with the numerals rotating under the fixed index. 'Start' puts the page into Orbit: the yellow ground turns graphite, the reading column narrows to 60ch, and the nav, screenshots and sticky price fade to 20%. The sticky rim shows the countdown (mm:ss, Rubik 600 tabular). At zero the bell line reads 'Session logged. Whatever's left rolls to tomorrow.' Esc or Stop exits, nothing is stored, and focus is never trapped. No-JS: the dial renders set to 25 with the printed line 'Focus Orbit: 25-minute default, configurable', and the slider controls are absent. Reduced motion: the ring snaps between values without spinning, Orbit changes colour instantly, and the countdown digits still update.
styles.motionGrammar: Mechanical and damped. The ring turns in 220ms ease-out steps of 5 minutes, with no inertia or flinging. When the day spiral first enters view its arcs draw clockwise over 600ms, and the Call dentist arc crosses onto the next turn last. Nothing else moves. Under prefers-reduced-motion the arcs render already drawn, the ring snaps, and Orbit switches instantly.
styles.readModeVariant: Privacy, support and alternatives keep the knurled cap nav and use the yellow body as the frame, with one white face panel as the reading column (Rubik 400 18px/1.65, 66ch). The title sits on the yellow in Rubik 700 44px ink, beside a small 25-dial mark. The privacy page opens with the base-label block of transparency figures, and the support page puts the developer email on the knob. Alternatives pages place a two-column comparison on the face ('Taskful Day | Streaks'), then 'Pick Taskful Day if… / Stick with Streaks if…' as two leaflet panels, then the FAQ, and end with the knob holding the badge.
styles.assetsNeeded: Nothing new is needed to ship. The dial scale, the day spiral and the leaflet diagrams are inline SVG and CSS drawn in code, and the screenshots already exist. Production follow-ups: real Focus Orbit, Day Clock, Energy River and Day Map screenshots and a Mac screenshot, plus corrected alt text for screenshots 2–6.
styles.risk: Pomodoro is productivity's most clichéd image, and a timer by itself speaks only for Focus Orbit, one of four views. If the day spiral doesn't carry the rollover, the page sells a timer app. A drenched yellow is loud for a 'calm' brand, so the white face and the graphite cap must take most of the reading. Text inside a circle wastes width, so long copy leaves the circle after the hero. Orbit mode must stay opt-in and fully escapable.
styles.memoryTest: A giant sun-yellow kitchen-timer dial with the App Store badge on the knob. Winding it to 25 dimmed the whole site into focus mode, and the unfinished dentist call spiralled past midnight into Tuesday.

notes: The roll ran degraded: the roll service was offline, so there were no catalog challengers and no quality-bar boards, but the dealt indices still bind. Key 3bead416 dealt ASSIGNED INDEX 7 (Now Showing, my lowest-ranked candidate), which became STYLE A 'THE ROLL'. Reroll 1 dealt 6 (Wind-Up Timer), distinct on the first try, which became STYLE C 'SECOND ROLL'. Neither roll was 1, so STYLE B is candidate 1, 'IMPECCABLE’S PICK'. Both dealt candidates sat at the bottom of my list, so I built each at full commitment by making it carry the rollover, not just a focus timer: the marquee uses the cinema's own HELD OVER convention, and the timer's dial grammar extends to a 24-hour spiral that crosses midnight. Sibling separation: allpaid already owns the wall planner and dry-erase marker world, so I left it alone. Earnlock's vending machine has a sage-enamel frame around a lit panel, so the marquee fascia is midnight blue, not green. Soon's 'Admit One' ticket stub is the nearest neighbour, so the marquee uses no tickets apart from the box-office tray. Blue is split across the three: A is blue-hour midnight, B uses ballpoint ink only, C is sun-yellow with blue only for the index. Faces: Big Shoulders Display (the studio's style A uses the separate Stencil cut), Cabin, Shantell Sans, Inclusive Sans and Rubik. I checked the existing sibling cards: none uses these in these roles. Albert Sans and Jost were dropped because pawza C and soon A use them. Font payloads: A ~63 KB, B ~120 KB, C ~76 KB. Before build: settle the four data conflicts in the evidence list (watchOS listed in platforms, Focus Orbit Free vs Pro, the Streaks price, 'no score' vs the analytics score), and correct the alt text on screenshots 2–6. No founder block exists, so the E-E-A-T line is the maker/freshness imprint only. With 4 ratings, no stars are shown in any style.

pageFixes.issue: Below the hero, the three styles of each surface follow one section order with new labels. appmeta-a ≡ appmeta-b, gymlogger-x-a ≡ -b ≡ -c, rightsplit-b ≡ -c, shogiful-b ≡ -c, wanderwiki-a ≡ -b (-c swaps two blocks) and pawza-a ≡ -c. The xiangqiful, earnlock and millrace trios each differ by one swap. Across the 60 microsite styles, one order dominates: hero → quick answer → (quick reference) → how it works → screenshots → features → who_for/who_not_for → price → comparison → privacy → founder/about → (roadmap) → FAQ → further reading → closing. That is one static structure in 60 costumes, which is the thing the owner refused ('do not use the same static structure for each page, build them from scratch'). It also makes the three styles per page skin choices, not page choices.
